data.title: Marimekko Oyj Just Beat Analyst Forecasts, And Analysts Have Been Updating Their Predictions
data.description:
Investors in Marimekko Oyj (HEL:MEKKO) had a good week, as its shares rose 5.1% to close at €9.60 following the release of its third-quarter results. Marimekko Oyj reported €52m in revenue, roughly in line with analyst forecasts, although statutory earnings per share (EPS) of €0.25 beat expectations, being 7.1% higher than what the analysts expected. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. So we collected the latest post-earnings statutory consensus estimates to see what could be in store for next year.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Following the latest results, Marimekko Oyj's five analysts are now forecasting revenues of €208.0m in 2027. This would be a meaningful 8.2% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to ascend 15% to €0.71. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of €207.6m and earnings per share (EPS) of €0.71 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Marimekko Oyj

With no major changes to earnings forecasts, the consensus price target fell 9.8% to €11.28, suggesting that the analysts might have previously been hoping for an earnings upgrade. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Marimekko Oyj at €12.00 per share, while the most bearish prices it at €10.60. Still, with such a tight range of estimates, it suggeststhe analysts have a pretty good idea of what they think the company is worth.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. The analysts are definitely expecting Marimekko Oyj's growth to accelerate, with the forecast 6.5% annualised growth to the end of 2027 ranking favourably alongside historical growth of 4.9% per annum over the past five years. Compare this with other companies in the same industry, which are forecast to grow their revenue 6.1% annually. Marimekko Oyj is expected to grow at about the same rate as its industry, so it's not clear that we can draw any conclusions from its growth relative to competitors.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. Happily, there were no real changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow in line with the overall industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of Marimekko Oyj's future valuation.

With that in mind, we wouldn't be too quick to come to a conclusion on Marimekko Oyj. Long-term earnings power is much more important than next year's profits. We have forecasts for Marimekko Oyj going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

Another thing to consider is whether management and directors have been buying or selling stock recently. We provide an overview of all open market stock trades for the last twelve months on our platform, here.

data.description:

  • The resolution coincides with reported preliminary third quarter YUTREPIA demand that management describes as positive. This points to operational focus shifting from courtroom risk to execution on commercialization and on cash commitments tied to the settlement.

The recent settlement keeps YUTREPIA on shelves while tying the business to defined net payments through April 2027, so the near term lens shifts toward execution, pricing, and payer conversion from voucher support to fully reimbursed use.

data.title: Vale Stock And Brazil Exporters Riding A Weaker Real
data.description:
Brazil’s weaker growth outlook and higher borrowing costs have hit local assets hard, yet the same mix has pushed the real lower and reshaped where risk and reward sit. That shift can punish highly indebted firms while creating openings for exporters with meaningful foreign currency revenue. This article unpacks how that tension plays out and walks through three Brazilian large caps that appear well exposed to this macro shock.

Vale (BOVESPA:VALE3)

Vale is the textbook example of this screener’s idea, a Brazilian mining giant that earns heavily in foreign currency while paying many of its bills in reais, so the weak currency backdrop is central to how investors think about its iron ore and metals franchise today.

Vale is a global miner focused on iron ore and nickel. Iron Ore Solutions generated about R$161.1b in revenue and Vale Base Metals contributed roughly R$54.8b. The group carries a market value near R$266.7b.

"The ramp up of copper projects in Carajás, including Bacaba and the Salobo coarse particle flotation program, together with other pipeline projects that aim to take Vale’s copper production to about 700,000 tons per year by 2035, can increase future revenue and EBITDA contribution from copper."

What really changes the risk reward here is how one pressure point on costs and cash generation resolves over the next few years.

Petroreconcavo (BOVESPA:RECV3)

Petroreconcavo taps directly into the weaker real theme, with oil and gas production priced off global benchmarks while much of the cost base sits in Brazil. As a result, its mature onshore fields become a pure test of execution and capital discipline under tougher macro conditions.

Petroreconcavo focuses on oil and gas extraction in Brazil, generating about R$3.0b from its E&P segment and carrying a market value near R$3.0b.

"The company has shifted its 2026 drilling mix toward lower risk projects while increasing the number of workover interventions and water injection projects, including 57 workovers and several new injectors completed in early 2026."

That pressure point is exactly where the story gets interesting. Read the full narrative for Petroreconcavo for how Petroreconcavo’s execution could turn current headwinds into leverage.

CSN Mineração (BOVESPA:CMIN3)

CSN Mineração plugs neatly into the weak real theme as a large iron ore exporter, turning foreign currency sales into Brazilian reais while running much of its cost base locally. The miner generates about R$17.4b from mining and carries a market value near R$26.5b.

data.title: XPEL Fell While Profit Rose
data.description:

Holding XPEL from the start of the year would have meant a 23.6% loss, including dividends. If you had made that call on 1 January, how would you judge it now, and what does that expansion plan really need to deliver by 2028?

Narratives are how investors here put a case on the record, with explicit assumptions about revenue, margins and the multiple. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

The Argument XPEL Investors Were Really Weighing

The shares cost US$49.91 at the start of the period, and anyone buying XPEL then had to choose between two very different but credible stories.

The bullish narrative put fair value at US$55. It relied on XPEL’s push into China and other high-volume channels, assuming revenue could grow 15.3% a year with margins rising from 10.8% to 16.4% by 2028.

The more cautious view set fair value at US$46.51. That thesis accepted expansion into emerging markets, but focused on risks from intensifying competition and OEMs offering factory-installed paint protection that could pressure margins.

What The Facts Did To The XPEL Thesis

XPEL’s US$110 million buildout in San Antonio and China clearly leaned toward the bullish case that assumed successful expansion into high volume markets. Quarterly evidence lined up with that story. Revenue and profit both rose between Q3 2025 and Q3 2026, and net margin increased from 10.3% to 11.9%, which challenged the more cautious margin view.

The lesson is simple. When a thesis hangs on expansion and profitability, track where the capital is going and then watch reported margins, not just headline growth or target prices.

What XPEL’s Lower Price Now Asks You To Believe

XPEL now trades at US$38.39, well below where the year began. The selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits above the current price and leans on the idea that today’s level underplays what a larger manufacturing base and richer sales mix could mean if they perform as intended.

The argument turns on XPEL converting its US$110 million buildout and higher margin channel mix into sustainably stronger profitability. A buyer today has to judge whether that shift toward window film, installation services, OEM and dealership volume can be maintained long enough for the Narrative’s higher figure to be justified.

"Increasing vertical integration through the planned US$110 million manufacturing and supply chain build out in San Antonio and China, supported by recent term debt and record operating cash flow, is expected to replace an asset light sourcing model with in house production that could structurally lift gross margin and operating margin as facilities ramp."

data.title: KH Group Oyj's (HEL:KHG) Soft Earnings Don't Show The Whole Picture
data.description:
KH Group Oyj's (HEL:KHG) earnings announcement last week didn't impress shareholders. However, our analysis suggests that the soft headline numbers are getting counterbalanced by some positive underlying factors.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Examining Cashflow Against KH Group Oyj's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

For the year to September 2026, KH Group Oyj had an accrual ratio of -0.19. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of €23m, well over the €1.38m it reported in profit. KH Group Oyj's free cash flow improved over the last year, which is generally good to see.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On KH Group Oyj's Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, KH Group Oyj produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Based on this observation, we consider it possible that KH Group Oyj's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! On the other hand, its EPS actually shrunk in the last twelve months. The goal of this article has been to assess how well we can rely on the statutory earnings to reflect the company's potential, but there is plenty more to consider. In light of this, if you'd like to do more analysis on the company, it's vital to be informed of the risks involved. For instance, we've identified 4 warning signs for KH Group Oyj (1 shouldn't be ignored) you should be familiar with.

Today we've zoomed in on a single data point to better understand the nature of KH Group Oyj's profit. But there are plenty of other ways to inform your opinion of a company.
